newsitem.title: USA: "Online households" seen reaching 66.6 mln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: "Online households" seen reaching 66.6 mln by 2000.

text.p: The number of worldwide "online households" -- personal computers or other devices in the home accessing online services and the Internet -- will rise to 66.6 million by the year 2000 from 23.4 million in 1996, the market research firm Jupiter Communications forecast on Monday.
Increased PC penetration, telecommunications deregulation, and deployment of ISDN (integrated services digital network) in Europe andd Asia will be the key factors driving growth, it said.
"The global market for online services is in position to grow tremendously over the next five years," said Kurt Abrahamson, managing director of New York-based Jupiter Communications.
